title: The seawall at seven
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Summer mornings: Wood draws the town from the seawall at seven before the shop or the drive. The same view. He decides to do it every morning for a week. Monday: the town, the fog in, the sign across the bay a gray shape.

panels.composition: The town from the seawall at seven AM: the four blocks, fog in, the Lanes' sign across 101 a gray shape, no letters. WOOD on the wall with the pad. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a small coastal town's main street seen from a seawall at seven in the morning with fog in and a distant sign as a gray shape, a young man drawing on the wall with a small dog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: the town in fog, the sign a rectangle, no letters. Monday, written small in the corner.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad showing a foggy town with a blank rectangle where a sign would be, black and white, no words

panels.composition: A passing FISHERMAN, early, looking at the pad. Not stopping. A nod.

image.prompt: a fisherman in boots walking past a young man drawing on a seawall and giving a nod, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The town. The fog. Wood small on the wall. Five mornings. The strip has a project and it's the view.

image.prompt: a young man small on a seawall drawing a foggy town in early light, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Monday: fog, the sign a rectangle. Five mornings, one view.
